card.name: Syllable dots inside dictionary headwords
card.fires_on: The separator or accented letter inside a word that is spelled out syllable by syllable or with special letters. Seen in dictionary entries such as im·pli·cate and in transliterated Greek or Latin etymologies.

modes.label: Syllable dots
modes.description: The middle dot between syllables in a dictionary-style hyphenation of a long word.

modes.label: Accented etymology letters
modes.description: An accented vowel inside a transliterated Greek or Latin word in an etymology note.

modes.label: Spaced-out letters
modes.description: A letter inside a word printed with spaces between its letters.
modes.example: L e uk o c y t<< e>> s / m m 3 P l

card.plain: It fires inside words broken into syllables or written with accented letters, as in dictionary entries and word origins.
